newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Deng's death spooks early Singapore stock market.
newsitem.headline: Deng's death spooks early Singapore stock market.

text.p: News of the death of Chinese paramount leader Deng Xiaoping spooked the Singapore stock market lower in early Thursday trade but dealers said the downside was likely to be limited.
"There will be some selling pressure but the market looks likely to rebound very quickly. Of course, we are not expecting a spike out of respect for Deng," said a dealer with a local house.
Another dealer said any weakness would be limited as Deng had not been actively on the scene since 1992.
After hitting a low of 2,236.53, the benchmark Straits Times Industrials Index traded towards 2,242.23 by 0125 GMT.
Its previous close was 2,246.99. Turnover was around 80 million shares with losers outpacing gainers by 181 to 47.
Dealers said buying on dips by institutions underpinned some blue chips while syndicate play supported Malaysian counters.
Frozen seafood trader Pacific Andes topped the actives with over 18 million shares. The price was up US$0.06 to US$0.63.

Fruit and vegetable supplier FHTK and Kian Ho Bearings stayed active on talk their share prices would test Singapore $0.90 (US$0.63) shortly. FHTK was up S$0.02 at S$0.79. Kian Ho was up S$0.01 at S$0.735.
